title: 🏛️ Exams 2001–2025 · writing prepared: describe, persuade, give your opinion ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, general) Task: "Write a twelve-line post on your Facebook page to encourage tourists to visit Tunisia and suggest it as the best destination for their holidays. State at least three sound arguments to persuade them." Which of these points are sound arguments for the post?

options.text: Its Mediterranean beaches are warm and sandy in summer.
The country has about eleven million inhabitants.
You can visit Roman sites such as Carthage and El Jem.
I am an influencer and many people follow my page.
Tunisians are welcoming and the food is delicious.
Some tourists prefer a holiday in cold countries.

questions.explanation: To persuade tourists, an argument must give them a reason to come: beaches, Roman sites to visit, and a warm welcome with good food. The number of inhabitants is a fact that gives no reason to travel, the number of followers is about the writer and not about the destination, and the last point is a reason to go somewhere else.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, general) Same post for tourists. Which opening sentence speaks to the readers and makes them want to read on?

options.text: I was born in Tunis and I live there with my family.
Tunisia is a country in North Africa on the Mediterranean Sea.
Looking for the perfect holiday place? Come to Tunisia!
Tourists must show their passports at the airport.

questions.explanation: A post that encourages must speak to the readers (you) and invite them to act: a question about their holidays followed by an invitation. A personal fact tells about the writer, a plain geographical fact informs without persuading, and a rule about passports has nothing to do with the wish to visit.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, technical) Task: "Write an 8-line article about the importance of using safety items to keep workers safe." What exactly must the article do?

options.text: Tell the story of a worker who had an accident last year.
Give the names of the shops that sell helmets and gloves.
Describe the inside of a workshop in detail.
Explain why safety items matter for workers' safety.

questions.explanation: The task is about the importance of safety items, so the article gives reasons: helmets, gloves and goggles prevent injuries and let workers do their job without danger. A story, a list of shops or a description of a workshop may mention safety, but none of them explains why it matters.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, general) Task: "…some of your classmates didn't like to join in. Write a 10-line article for your school magazine to convince them to take part in this voluntary work." Which argument answers the classmates who refuse?

options.text: The headmaster will punish every pupil who does not come to help with the work.
Working in a group is quick and fun, and everybody enjoys a clean school.
Rubbish is a big problem in many countries of the world, and it keeps growing.
Last year I planted a tree in my garden and I was very happy that whole day.

questions.explanation: To convince someone who refuses, the writer gives a reason that changes their mind: the work is fast, pleasant, and brings a benefit to everybody. A threat of punishment forces but does not convince, a general fact about rubbish does not speak to the classmates' reluctance, and one personal memory is too narrow to prove anything to others.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, technical) Task: "Write an 8-line article for this magazine in which you describe the best house design that will help you get the prize." Which details belong in the description?

options.text: a large living room with big windows that look onto the garden
solar panels on the roof to save electricity
a story about the day my uncle built his own house
three bedrooms, one with a desk for homework
You should buy this magazine every month.
a kitchen open to the dining area

questions.explanation: A description says what the house looks like and what it offers: the living room, the solar panels, the bedrooms and the kitchen are features of the design. A story about an uncle tells an event instead of describing, and advice to buy the magazine is addressed to readers, not part of the house.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2020, general) "They keep complaining about long school hours, exams, homework, lack of leisure activities and violence." You describe the school of your dreams. Match each complaint with the feature of the dream school that answers it.

options.text: long school hours
lack of leisure activities
violence
homework
a club for music, sport and drama every afternoon
light tasks given only when they help to learn
a short day that ends at two o'clock
teachers and pupils who settle problems by talking

questions.explanation: A description of a dream school answers each complaint with its opposite: shorter days against long hours, clubs against the lack of leisure, dialogue against violence, and light, useful tasks against heavy homework.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2017, general) You give a speech to thank your parents after the national exam. The frame starts with "Dear Mum and Dad," and ends with "Your loving son/daughter". Which ending is right for the speech?

options.text: I hereby declare that I am grateful. Yours faithfully, a pupil
That is all for today. Goodbye, boys and girls.
Thank you for everything. Your loving son/daughter, Karim Ben Salah
Thank you for everything. Your loving son/daughter

questions.explanation: The speech is warm and addressed to the parents: it ends with a thank-you and the printed family formula. A formal ending such as "Yours faithfully" does not fit a speech to one's parents, "boys and girls" speaks to the wrong people, and the exam says not to write a name or to sign, so adding one breaks the rule.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015, general) Task: write a ten-line article to encourage your schoolmates to volunteer and take action. Hints: "donate – stand by – give hope – support – raise – collect – join". Which sentence uses a hint to encourage readers?

options.text: Join us and donate a little of your pocket money to help needy people!
The hints are donate, stand by, give hope, support, raise, collect and join.
The campaign collected a lot of clothes last winter.
Some people donated money to the charity last year.

questions.explanation: The task is to encourage: the sentence must speak to schoolmates and ask them to act, as the imperative with "Join" and "donate" does. The other sentences contain hint words, but one copies the list and two only report what others did, which informs and does not push anyone to volunteer.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2001) Your parents cannot decide whether to live in the city or in the countryside. "What do you prefer? Give your reasons." Which sentence gives a preference with a reason?

options.text: I prefer the countryside.
I prefer the countryside because the air is clean and it is quiet.
The city and the countryside are two different places.
I prefer the countryside, and my cousin lives in a big house in the city where he goes to the cinema every week.

questions.explanation: The task asks for a preference and its reasons: one choice, then a reason introduced by "because". A bare preference gives no reason, a sentence that only says the two places differ does not choose, and a long sentence about the cousin's life in the city supports the opposite choice.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2001) You write a short paragraph on the same task and choose the city. Put these sentences in the order of a clear paragraph.

options.text: Then, buses and trains take us everywhere easily.
First, schools, hospitals and libraries are close to home.
I would prefer to live in the city.
For these reasons, I would choose the city.

questions.explanation: The paragraph starts with the choice, gives the reasons in order with First and Then, and ends with a closing sentence introduced by "For these reasons".
